# EnterpriseGlue v0.36.1 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.36.0`.

## Highlights

- **cloud-authentication:** Allow verified email links to establish managed Cloud sessions and protect link requests with optional Turnstile verification.
- **git:** Seed an active GitHub provider when a managed Cloud tenant is created.

## User and administrator impact

- An account can sign in by email link and add a passkey afterward.
- Email signup refuses known disposable email domains.
- New managed Cloud organizations can select GitHub when connecting a repository.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Deploy the shared and host packages from the same qualified release.

## API and integration compatibility

- Adds public email challenge configuration and an email proof completion endpoint.
- Adds an optional passkey registration flow for verified Cloud email sessions.

## Configuration

- Set EG_CLOUD_EMAIL_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and EG_CLOUD_EMAIL_TURNSTILE_SECRET together to enable server verification.
- Set EG_FRONTEND_CLOUD_EMAIL_TURNSTILE_ENABLED=true on the matching frontend image.
- Set cloudEmailSignupProtection.enabled, siteKey and the dedicated secret reference in split-runtime Helm deployments.
- The default GitHub provider uses the configured OAuth client when one is available. Personal access token support remains available.

## Database migrations

- The provider record and the new organization are written in the same transaction and tenant scope.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Email proofs and Turnstile tokens are single-use.
- Administrator eligibility is rechecked for email-only sessions.
- The provider remains subject to the existing tenant isolation and connection authorization checks.

## Documentation

- docs/reference/configuration.md
- docs/architecture/postgresql-context-boundary.md

## Known limitations

- Existing organizations retain their configured providers.

## Rollback

- Restore the prior host and frontend together.
- Use the previous qualified host. Any provider records created before rollback remain scoped to their organizations.

## Validation evidence

- Targeted authentication, frontend, deployment and PostgreSQL isolation tests passed.
- Focused tenant-service and restricted PostgreSQL tests cover the new default, existing self-hosted seeding and transaction rollback.
